Article Title: Canadian billionaire Kevin O’Leary says success takes sacrifice, focus, and an obsession with getting ...
Article Text:
Read Kevin O’Leary’s complete post here

Lessons from other business leaders

Kevin O’Leary gives a blunt warning to startup founders

Canadian billionaire and former Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary has shared his perspective on what it takes to achieve success at the highest level. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) O’Leary argued that people striving for exceptional results should not expect balance in life. “There is no balance when you are trying to win at the highest level,” he wrote. “Success takes sacrifice, focus and an obsession with getting the few things that actually matter done.” Along with this, he also urged the individuals to identify their three to five top priorities and also avoid distractions that could derail their goals. “If you can identify your three to five priorities and refuse to let anything distract you from them, you are already operating differently than most people,” O’Leary added.“There is no balance when you are trying to win at the highest level. Success takes sacrifice, focus, and an obsession with getting the few things that actually matter done. If you can identify your three to five priorities and refuse to let anything distract you from them, you are already operating differently than most people.”O’Leary’s comments echo similar advice from other prominent entrepreneurs. Paul Graham, co-founder of Y Combinator, recently argued that startup growth can help founders solve business problems and guide product development, starting with minimal products and adding features that drive growth.Earlier, billionaire Mark Cuban emphasized that wealth requires sacrifice, discipline, and aggressive saving. He advised cutting unnecessary expenses, saving consistently, and keeping cash accessible for opportunities.Meanwhile, Elon Musk recalled Tesla’s near-collapse during the 2008 financial crisis, noting that survival required emergency funding and a workforce deeply committed to the company’s mission. Musk stressed the importance of pushing through difficult periods and hiring employees who believe in the mission.In another news, recently O’Leary delivered a sharp warning to startup founders, according to a report by Benzinga. O’Leary has urged the startup founders to recognise their failure early and avoid pouring more money into businesses that are not working. Sharing his advice on X, O’Leary said: “The worst mistake you can make as an entrepreneur is refusing to admit when something has failed.” O’Leary also cautioned that continued spending cannot turn an unsuccessful concept into a viable business. “Bad ideas do not become good ideas just because you keep throwing more money at them,” he wrote. Instead, he advised founders to embrace losses, learn from them, and move on. He added: “80% of startups fail. You cannot cry about every one.”
Article Summary: Canadian billionaire Kevin O’Leary has shared his perspective on what it takes to achieve success at the highest level. He urged the individuals to identify their three to five top priorities and also avoid distractions that could derail their goals. O'Leary’s comments echo similar advice from other prominent entrepreneurs such as Mark Cuban and Elon Musk.

Article Title: Mysterious yacht docked at LA harbor for days, Instagrammers and Reddit users track the A-list owner who is …
Article Text:
Maritime data, social media users uncover the clues on ownership

What is inside JK Rowling’s $150 million mega-vessel

A massive luxury vessel parked in Marina del Rey all week has triggered intense curiosity across social media. The superyacht pulled into the Los Angeles harbor a few days ago, shrouded in secrecy. Harbor watchers immediately noticed that the vessel’s identifying nameplate had been concealed upon arrival, an uncommon move that quickly caught the attention of local boaters. However, locals and internet investigators identified the high-profile owner as Harry Potter creator J.K. Rowling.The California Post noted (via the New York Post) that the 290-foot mega-craft belongs to the 61-year-old British author. Despite efforts by the crew to mask the vessel's identity, harbor residents considered her arrival an open secret, with one observer calling it the worst-kept secret in the entire marina.The ship’s arrival quickly gained traction after being documented by the boating Instagram account twogirls.oneboat. Comment sections on Reddit and Instagram lit up with details from marina regulars. One social media commenter pointed out that local harbor captains recognised the vessel as Rowling’s yacht, named Samsara, noting that the nameplate gets covered to avoid drawing organised demonstrations.Another commenter recalled that the same yacht stopped at the marina last May, where the crew similarly masked the moniker and turned off its AIS tracking signal due to public backlash surrounding Rowling's activism. Moreover, maritime data from Marine Traffic verifies the boat’s location in Marina del Rey.Constructed in 2015 by custom shipyard Oceanco, the yacht began its journey as Infinity under its first owner, Harbor Freight Tools chief executive Eric Smidt. Australian billionaire Brett Blundy acquired the vessel in 2022 before selling it to Rowling in 2023, who rechristened the vessel Samsara.Estimated to be worth roughly $150 million, the yacht houses 26 crew members and accommodates more than 12 guests. According to SuperYachtFan.com, its onboard amenities include a private cinema, a tranquil beach club and a circular outdoor pool.The yacht has previously drawn headlines with Rowling igniting backlash from the deck of Samsara in 2025 after posting a cigar-smoking photo. Later that year, an image of the yacht refueling in Port Angeles, Washington, spurred heated Reddit threads attacking the craft’s environmental footprint.

Article Title: Man who ‘protects’ employees of Salesforce, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta are planning to go on strike as ...
Article Text:
Why staff is organising demonstrations

Unionised security officers tasked with guarding the California headquarters and regional facilities of top tech giants, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and Salesforce, have formally voted to authorise a strike to demand higher compensation and improved workplace benefits. The collective bargaining action has been announced by the SEIU-United Service Workers West (SEIU-USWW), which represents approximately 14,000 security specialists across Los Angeles County, Silicon Valley and the broader San Francisco Bay Area.According to a report by the New York Post, the affected guards work for third-party staffing contractors, primarily Allied Universal, GardaWorld and Securitas, that provide daily physical defense and building access control for Silicon Valley’s largest corporate facilities. In a statement distributed through the union, Hayward-based Allied Universal guard Christopher Yates called on contractor leadership to negotiate in good faith:“We're asking Allied and the other security companies to stop playing games, come to the table, and settle a strong contract with real raises, better training, and respect for the officers who keep these buildings safe.”To signal their resolve, security guards marched through downtown San Francisco on Wednesday (September 2), passing directly near the corporate campuses of both Anthropic and OpenAI. While the union has officially approved an unfair-labor-practice strike, labor representatives have not confirmed an exact walkout date or whether an outright work stoppage is inevitable.Anticipating labor unrest, Anthropic instructed its San Francisco workforce to work remotely last week over expectations of an imminent walkout by Allied Universal security guards.The potential walkout arrives as physical security risks around AI companies reach new highs, forcing tech firms to significantly upgrade on-site protective measures.Both Anthropic and OpenAI have faced multiple direct threats aimed at their staff members. In one high-profile incident in April, law enforcement officials reported that an explosive Molotov cocktail was hurled directly into the private residence of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , who subsequently pointed to heightened anti-AI rhetoric as a likely factor behind the violent assault.
Article Summary: Security guards at tech firms including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and Salesforce have voted to strike. They are demanding higher compensation and improved workplace benefits. Security guards marched through downtown San Francisco on Wednesday (September 2), passing directly near the corporate campuses of both Anthropic and OpenAI.

Which HBCUs has MacKenzie Scott donated to

Why Mackenzie Scott’s donations stand out

MacKenzie Scott has set a new milestone in her philanthropy to historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs), with her latest donations taking her total giving to the institutions to more than $1 billion. The former wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos , who sold about half of her Amazon stake in 2020, has given tens of millions of dollars to individual HBCUs, including a $42 million gift to Elizabeth City State University that pushed her total HBCU donations past the $1 billion mark.MacKenzie Scott’s $42 million donation to Elizabeth City State University in North Carolina was made earlier this year on the university’s Founders Day. The gift took her total donations to HBCUs to well over $1 billion.Elizabeth City State University Chancellor S. Keith Hargrove thanked Scott for the donation and said it would support the university’s ASCEND 2030 strategic plan.Scott’s giving to HBCUs is part of a wider philanthropic effort. Since 2020, she has committed about $26 billion to thousands of organisations working across areas including education, health, community development, disaster recovery and environmental causes.Scott has made several large donations to HBCUs over the past six years. In November 2025, she gave Howard University $80 million. The donation was among the largest in the university’s 158-year history.She has also donated to institutions including Morgan State University, Prairie View A&M University, Norfolk State University, Bowie State University, Virginia State University and Winston-Salem State University.In 2025, Scott also donated $70 million each to the Thurgood Marshall College Fund and the United Negro College Fund.MacKenzie Scott’s HBCU donations include:Her donations have also gone to schools including Hampton University, Morehouse College, North Carolina A&T State University, Tuskegee University, Xavier University of Louisiana and the University of Maryland Eastern Shore.Many of Scott’s donations are unrestricted. This means universities can decide how to use the money instead of following conditions set by the donor. The funds can be used for scholarships, faculty hiring, endowments, campus upgrades or other priorities identified by the universities.Scott has previously described her approach to giving as based on trust and direct support for organisations.
Article Summary: MacKenzie Scott’s $42 million donation to Elizabeth City State University in North Carolina was made earlier this year. The gift took her total donations to HBCUs to well over $1 billion. Since 2020, she has committed about $26 billion to thousands of organisations working across areas including education, health, community development and environmental causes.

Article Title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said that he is willing to wait to have kids till Elon Musk’s Neuralink ...
Article Text:
Why Alexandr Wang wants to wait for Neuralink before having kids

Why Alexandr Wang believes children could adapt better

Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI chief and highest paid employee, has said he is willing to wait to have children until brain-computer interfaces such as Elon Musk’s Neuralink become more advanced. Wang made the comments during an appearance on the Shawn Ryan Show last year while discussing the future of AI, human development and brain-computer interfaces. He said he wants to wait until Neuralink or similar technology “start working” before having kids. “I want to wait to have kids until we figure out how Neuralink or other … start working,” Alexandr Wang said during the podcast.Wang’s reason is linked to how he believes children’s brains could adapt to the technology. During the podcast, he explained that the first several years of a child’s life are an important period for brain development. He argued that the high level of neuroplasticity during childhood could allow children who grow up with brain-computer interfaces to use the technology in ways that adults may not be able to.“In your first like seven years of life, your brain is more neuroplastic than at any other point in your life, like by an order of magnitude,” Wang said.He then compared the idea with how children develop their ability to process information from their senses.Alexandr Wang described a case involving children born with cataracts. He said that if the cataracts prevent a child from seeing during the early years of development, removing them later may not allow the child to develop normal vision because the brain did not learn to process signals from the eyes during the key period.His view is that a similar effect could eventually apply to brain-computer interfaces. “When we get Neuralink and we get these other technologies, kids who are born with them are going to learn how to use them in like, crazy, crazy ways,” Wang said.Wang said a brain-computer interface could eventually become integrated into the way a person's brain works if it is introduced early enough. He believes this could be different for adults who receive an implant later in life.“It'll be a actually like a part of their brain in a way that it'll never be true for an adult who gets like a neural link or whatever, hooked into their brain,” he said.The Meta AI chief also connected his thinking about brain-computer interfaces to the rapid development of artificial intelligence. “I believe a lot in AI,” Wang said, adding that he expects AI to become “smarter and smarter, more and more capable, more and more powerful.”He said AI could eventually take different forms, including robots and other systems.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI chief and highest paid employee, has said he is willing to wait to have children until brain-computer interfaces become more advanced. Wang made the comments during an appearance on the Shawn Ryan Show last year. He said he wants to wait until Neuralink or similar technology “start working” before having kids.

Article Title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison’s first wife filed for divorce 3 months after their daughter's birth; but he was 'determined to remain friends' as ...
Article Text:
Larry Ellison's reflection on the split

Life after the divorce

Oracle founder Larry Ellison faced a personal turning point in 1986 when his first wife, Barbra, filed for divorce just three months after the birth of their daughter, Megan. According to a report by People.com, the split came at a pivotal time in Ellison’s life as he was balancing the early growth of Oracle with the new family responsibilities. Ellison and Boothe, who met while she worked as a receptionist at Relational Software Inc. — the company that would later become Oracle — married in 1983. Their son, David, was born in January of that year, followed three years later by their daughter, Megan, born January 31, 1986.Barbara filed for divorce in April 1986, just three months after Megan's birth, bringing the three-year marriage to an end.In Matthew Symonds' 2003 book "Softwar: An Intimate Portrait of Larry Ellison and Oracle," Ellison said he was determined to remain friends with his ex-wife for the sake of raising healthy, happy children. He also reflected on how fatherhood had reshaped him personally, saying becoming a father fundamentally changed his personality, made him more sensitive to his children's needs and feelings, and gradually made him a more considerate friend and partner more broadly. He described the experience simply as growing up.After the split, Barbara took over the role of primary caregiver, raising David and Megan largely away from the spotlight of Ellison's rapidly growing tech fortune.She instilled in both children an early love of film, reportedly building a collection of more than 3,000 VHS tapes that the siblings would watch repeatedly, including favorites like "Jurassic Park" and "Back to the Future."That shared love of movies would go on to shape both siblings' adult careers. David Ellison founded Skydance Media, the production company behind franchises including "Mission: Impossible" and "Top Gun: Maverick." Megan Ellison founded Annapurna Pictures, which has produced acclaimed films such as "Zero Dark Thirty," "Her," and "American Hustle," earning her multiple Academy Award nominations along the way.Ellison, now one of the world’s wealthiest individuals, has been married and divorced multiple times.
Article Summary: Oracle founder Larry Ellison faced a personal turning point in 1986 when his first wife, Barbra, filed for divorce just three months after the birth of their daughter, Megan. Ellison and Boothe, who met while she worked as a receptionist at Relational Software Inc. — the company that would later become Oracle — married in 1983.

Article Title: From Florida to California, Americans are vandalising his cameras; now Flock CEO says: It's easier to pick a villain that's a…
Article Text:
Flock CEO Garrett Langley admits his cameras have become an easy target as Florida orders licence plate readers off state highways and cancellations pile up.

Florida's highway order is the widest government action yet against licence plate readers

Flock contract cancellations are accelerating, not slowing down

Flock's new privacy settings have not convinced the ACLU or the EFF

Garrett Langley's company has roughly 120,000 licence plate cameras bolted to poles across the United States, and 2026 has turned into the year Americans started pulling them down. Councils are voting contracts out. Residents in several states have covered lenses, wrapped poles, and in a few cases removed the hardware entirely. In Ohio last month, a grand jury declined to indict a man who had been filmed destroying a Flock pole.The Flock Safety chief executive has spent the past three weeks apologising, conceding and rewriting his product defaults. Asked whether the safeguards should have arrived sooner, he agreed they should have. But he also thinks the anger has found a convenient target. Because his cameras are visible in a way that most surveillance is not, he said, "it's easier to pick a villain that's a company like us."Florida's transport department revoked permission for police to operate automated licence plate readers on state highway rights of way, giving agencies 30 days to take them down. The order covers the entire category, including cameras from rivals Axon and Motorola, and cites misuse reports and privacy concerns.Jacksonville's sheriff dropped the technology across Duval County immediately, and Pasco and Manatee counties have moved to ban or remove the devices. Governor Ron DeSantis had flagged the move days earlier, saying "I think it's capturing way more information than they're letting on."Texas ordered state agencies to stop funding the cameras days earlier, after an officer in Lufkin was indicted on 100 felony counts over unauthorised database searches. A Wisconsin mayor had every camera in Menasha covered, and a Tennessee sheriff paused 70 readers. An Oakland advocacy group counts 214 cities and counties that have dropped Flock since 2021, with 93 of those in August alone, four times July's number. Its director said the chart had "gone parabolic".Flock's own framing is that arrivals outnumber exits. A spokesperson said new city partnerships have outpaced non-renewals by about ten to one this year, and the company claims more than 5,000 communities as customers. Langley puts the ratio closer to seven to one, and says cities that skip his cameras are choosing to be less safe.In August the company cut default data retention from 30 days to seven, said it will require every law enforcement customer to switch on its abuse detection tool by the end of the year, added automatic lockouts for abnormal searches, and made case codes mandatory. Langley wrote that abuse of the technology, at any level, is unacceptable.Critics are not sold. The ACLU wants an outside evaluator and has asked whether the tool is "a real security measure or just window dressing". A civil liberties lawyer noted that an officer can simply enter any case number and keep searching. Retention can be extended anyway through a setting called Evidence Mode.Langley's answer to all of it is compromise, his word, between safety and privacy. He has said "we're not Big Brother" and warned officers who abuse the system that "You will get caught, plain and simple." The people currently cutting his poles down are not waiting to find out.
Article Summary: 2026 has turned into the year Americans started pulling them down. Residents in several states have covered lenses, wrapped poles, and in a few cases removed the hardware. Florida's highway order is the widest government action yet against licence plate readers.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Marc Benioff: One day someone is your subordinate; the next day he or she may be your superior
Article Text:
Salesforce founder Marc Benioff

Marc Benioff's quote about business and relationships

Marc Benioff compares business to tennis

What happens when the person working for you today becomes your boss tomorrow? Salesforce founder and CEO Marc Benioff says that is one of the realities of business. In a quote about changing professional relationships, Marc Benioff highlighted how quickly roles can change in the workplace. “One day you compete. The next day you partner. One day someone is your subordinate; the next day he or she may be your superior,” he said. Benioff also pointed to a Japanese belief that business is temporary, while relationships can last. His words offer a simple view of how careers can change and why professional relationships can matter beyond a single job or business deal.Benioff's statement begins with the idea that business relationships are not always permanent. He referred to a Japanese belief that “business is temporal, whereas relationships are eternal.”“There is a Japanese belief that business is temporal, whereas relationships are eternal. That’s true. One day you compete. The next day you partner. One day someone is your subordinate; the next day he or she may be your superior. At its finest, business is friendly competition, just like a game of tennis,” he said.In the quote, Marc Benioff compared business competition with a game of tennis.“At its finest, business is friendly competition, just like a game of tennis,” he said.The comparison presents competition as something that does not have to end a relationship. A tennis match has two players competing against each other, but the competition exists within the rules of the game. Once the match ends, the relationship between the players can continue.Marc Benioff's quote puts a similar idea into the context of business. Careers and company relationships can change, but the people involved may continue to cross paths in new roles.For professionals, that can mean the person sitting across the table today could be working alongside them tomorrow — or could eventually become their boss.
Article Summary: Marc Benioff compared business competition with a game of tennis. “One day you compete. The next day you partner. One day someone is your subordinate; the next day he or she may be your superior,” he said. BenioFF also pointed to a Japanese belief that business is temporary, while relationships can last.

Article Title: Europe's biggest car company Volkswagen is laying off 100,000, reasons of job cuts have links going up to to China and the US
Article Text:
Volkswagen’s ‘future plan’

Volkwagen job cuts: Links to China and the US

Plant closures and a smaller lineup

Europe’s biggest car company Volkswagen has reportedly unanimously approved a sweeping transformation plan that will bring the automaker's total planned job cuts to 100,000, marking the most extensive restructuring in the company's 89-year history. According to a report by multiple sources and Reuters, this decision of the carmaker comes as part of sweeping transformation plan approved by the company’s supervisory board, which is aimed at reshaping operations and reducing costs.The board signed off on the "Future Plan," a package of a dozen initiatives aimed at making Europe's largest carmaker leaner and more competitive. The newly approved phase targets roughly 50,000 positions, including management roles, on top of another 50,000 cuts already agreed upon earlier this year. Combined, the reductions amount to roughly 15% of a global workforce that stood at more than 660,000 employees in 2025, and would eclipse the scale of General Motors' cuts following its 2009 bankruptcy.Volkswagen said the additional workforce reduction was necessary, beyond its existing cost-cutting programs, to safeguard the group's competitiveness going forward. The company has not detailed exactly when the cuts will take effect or how they will be distributed across its various brands and regions, though the plan is expected to unfold through the end of the decade.The job cuts stem from a mix of pressures bearing down on Volkswagen from multiple directions. The company is grappling with intensifying competition from Chinese automakers, both in China itself — long one of Volkswagen's most important markets — and increasingly in Europe, where Chinese electric-vehicle makers have been gaining ground. At the same time, Volkswagen has had to contend with US tariffs on imported vehicles, adding cost pressure just as global demand patterns shift and the industry pushes through a difficult technological transition toward electrification.Those headwinds have weighed heavily on sales. Volkswagen is expected to sell only about 8.5 million vehicles this year, down from 8.9 million in 2025, according to a supervisory board document reported by German outlet WirtschaftsWoche.As part of the overhaul, Volkswagen will halve its model lineup by 2035 and is examining alternative uses for four German plants — in Hannover, Emden, Zwickau and Neckarsulm — where no confirmed production plans exist for the next decade. Closing any of the sites outright would mark the first time Volkswagen has shut a full-scale factory on home soil. The company is also aiming to streamline its complex corporate structure and reduce the supervisory board's influence over major executive decisions. Porsche, part of the wider Volkswagen Group, is separately expected to cut around a fifth of its jobs by 2035.
Article Summary: Volkswagen's supervisory board reportedly approved a sweeping transformation plan that will bring the automaker's total planned job cuts to 100,000. The newly approved phase targets roughly 50,000 positions, including management roles. The company is grappling with intensifying competition from Chinese automakers, both in China itself and increasingly in Europe.

Officials across federal agencies in Trump administration sending mixed signals on Anthropic

Thank you for your attention to this matter!” Michael posted.The assessment from defense leadership directly contradicts optimistic statements made just a day prior by Lutnick during the G20 Innovation Summit. Speaking with Axios, Lutnick stated that the administration trusts Anthropic and its CEO, Dario Amodei, declaring: “They've done what we asked. They're back on the right side. So the answer is: Yes.”The conflicting messages appear to highlight friction across federal agencies following months of bitter disagreements regarding military deployment parameters for the company’s AI systems.Leadership tensions involving Amodei had deepened early-year disputes with the administration.Axios reported that to ease friction, Anthropic elevated co-founder Tom Brown to head high-level diplomatic outreach with White House officials.While a federal judge in August overturned the Pentagon’s prior move blacklisting Anthropic as a supply chain hazard, ruling that the action violated constitutional standards, “illegal and baseless”, the startup remains locked in an ongoing appeal. The company argued in the lawsuit that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth overstepped his authority with the new designation.Anthropic is currently challenging another separate Pentagon penalty levied under an alternative statute before the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. All the action against Anthropic followed after the company refused to allow the military to use its AI models for tasks including surveillance or autonomous weapons.
Article Summary: Pentagon official Emil Michael pushed back against notions of a complete reconciliation, taking to social media platform X (formerly Twitter) to reaffirm the Department of Defense’s cautious stance toward the company. The assessment from defense leadership directly contradicts optimistic statements made just a day prior by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Article Title: Uber layoffs: As company cuts 3,300 jobs, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi borrows two moves from Amazon CEO Andy Jassy; tells employees you spend too much time on...
Article Text:
Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi is cutting 3,300 jobs, about 10% of the company's global workforce, in its biggest restructuring in years.

Uber layoffs 2026: what the 3,300 job cuts actually change inside the company

Fewer managers and a return-to-office push: the Andy Jassy playbook Dara Khosrowshahi is copying

Why Uber's CEO did not blame AI for the layoffs, unlike Amazon, Meta and Block

Uber is cutting roughly 3,300 jobs, about 10% of its global workforce, in the biggest restructuring the ride-hailing giant has attempted in years. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi announced the layoffs in an internal email on September 2, later published on Uber's newsroom, and the framing will sound oddly familiar to anyone who has followed Amazon over the past two years. Fewer management layers. More individual contributors. Almost everyone back in an office. The cuts bring Uber's headcount down to just under 30,000, roughly where it stood in 2021, before the company's most recent expansion phase.The line employees are circulating is this one: "I'm sure many of you have felt that you spend too much time 'aligning' rather than building, shipping, or serving customers." Khosrowshahi says Uber heard this repeatedly in Pulse surveys and internal conversations. His fix is structural. Cut the coordinators, broaden manager scopes, and pull teams into fewer physical hubs. Investors liked it. Uber shares rose nearly 2% after the announcement, and analysts estimate the restructuring could free up as much as $2 billion in annual savings.The specifics matter more than the headline percentage. Uber has reduced the number of employees sitting seven or more layers below the CEO by 20%, and halved the number of "micro-teams," groups with just one or two direct reports.Roles focused primarily on coordination were the first to go, and the remit of the coordination jobs that survive has been narrowed.There is consolidation too. Uber is folding its three Delivery Ops teams (Restaurants, Retail and Direct) into single-threaded teams at global, regional and country level, putting the P&Ls under single owners. In Tech, Core Services Engineering and Science teams are being merged, mirroring a structure Mobility and Delivery already use. Everyone affected has already been notified, except in countries with mandatory local consultation processes.The two borrowed moves are hard to miss. In September 2024, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy told staff he wanted each S-team organisation to increase its ratio of individual contributors to managers by at least 15% by the end of Q1 2025. In the same memo, he ended hybrid work with a five-day return-to-office mandate effective January 2, 2025. Jassy even set up a "bureaucracy mailbox," which drew over 1,000 emails in six months and led to 375 process changes.Khosrowshahi is running the same two plays. Uber is asking the vast majority of remote employees to relocate to an office, leaving under 1% fully remote, and reinforcing its three-days-a-week hybrid policy, stricter than before but still short of Amazon's five. Global teams concentrate in New York and San Francisco; regional, local and tech teams get their own designated hubs. Managers will be co-located with their reports wherever possible, with early-career employees prioritised.Amazon's version of this has since escalated. Beth Galetti announced roughly 14,000 corporate role cuts in October, then another 16,000 in January 2026, describing both as continuations of the same layers-and-ownership work Jassy started.Here's where Uber diverges. Amazon has been explicit: Jassy wrote in June 2025 that generative AI and agents would mean "fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today," and that corporate headcount would shrink as a result. Galetti's October note called this generation of AI the most transformative technology since the internet.Khosrowshahi's memo doesn't mention AI as a cause at all. He attributes the cuts to complexity that accumulated while Uber's top line nearly tripled over five years. That's a notable choice in a year when Meta, Coinbase and Block have all cited AI while cutting staff, a rationale some analysts have suggested is convenient cover for margin repair or correcting old hiring mistakes.What Uber is spending on instead is autonomous driving. The company is expanding robotaxi partnerships, has launched autonomous rides in the UK with Wayve, and wants to build the largest self-driving platform. Savings from the cuts get reinvested there. Khosrowshahi says he made one big change rather than several small ones deliberately, so the disruption ends quickly.
Article Summary: Uber is cutting roughly 3,300 jobs, about 10% of its global workforce. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi announced the layoffs in an internal email on September 2. The framing will sound oddly familiar to anyone who has followed Amazon over the past two years.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Satya Nadella: “So long as you enjoy it, do it mindfully and…” - a reminder about finding meaning in your work
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Satya Nadella

“So long as you enjoy it, do it mindfully and well, and have an honest purpose behind it — life won't fail you.”

Meaning behind Satya Nadella's quote on work and purpose

Why taking your work seriously can turn interest into real skill

Why the process itself can be a source of satisfaction

Importance of mindfulness

What the quote can mean for a working life

Lessons learnt from Satya Nadella's quote

Enjoy what you do: Finding genuine interest in your work can make the effort more meaningful and easier to sustain over time.

Give your work proper attention: Being mindful means staying present, thinking carefully and not simply rushing through tasks.

Take pride in doing things well: Enjoyment becomes more valuable when it is supported by effort, discipline and a willingness to improve.

Have a genuine purpose: Knowing why you are doing something can help you stay grounded when progress is slow or circumstances change.

Do not measure everything by the outcome: Success does not always arrive in the form expected. The quality of the effort and the meaning behind it also matter.

Keep learning: Becoming good at something is not a final destination. Curiosity and continued learning can help turn an interest into lasting ability.

Choose your own definition of success: Career decisions do not have to be based entirely on money, status or recognition. What matters personally can be part of the equation too.

Accept that difficult periods are part of the process: Enjoying your work does not mean every task will be enjoyable. Frustration, repetition and setbacks can exist alongside genuine satisfaction.

Work is often measured by what it produces: a salary, a promotion, a finished project or a place on the next rung of the career ladder. But Satya Nadella has offered a simpler way to think about what makes work worthwhile. The Microsoft chief executive’s advice brings together three things that are not always discussed in the same breath: enjoying what you do, paying attention to how you do it and having a genuine reason for doing it. Rather than treating achievement as the only measure of progress, his perspective places greater weight on the quality and intention behind everyday effort.His words, “So long as you enjoy it, do it mindfully and well, and have an honest purpose behind it, life won't fail you,” are less about chasing a particular definition of success and more about the way a person approaches their choices. Behind the quote is an idea that applies beyond the workplace: doing something with care and purpose may matter just as much as where it eventually leads.The wording brings several ideas together. Enjoyment is the first condition, but it is not presented as a licence to simply follow whatever feels pleasant at the moment.There is also an expectation of attention: to do something mindfully means being present enough to understand what the work requires and what effect it has.Then comes the question of doing it well. Enjoying a task, in this sense, does not remove the need for discipline or competence. The quote places enjoyment beside effort rather than putting the two in opposition.The final part concerns purpose. Nadella's reference to an “honest purpose” gives the statement a more practical edge. A person's reason for doing something matters, particularly when the work becomes difficult or when recognition does not arrive quickly.The phrase “life won't fail you” can therefore be read less as a guarantee of a particular outcome and more as a reflection on the value of the process itself. Circumstances can remain uncertain. The result of an effort cannot always be controlled. What can be shaped, at least to some extent, is the manner in which a person chooses to work.There is a difference between being interested in something and taking it seriously. Interest can get a person started, but sustained attention is what turns that interest into a skill.That distinction is useful in the context of Nadella's career. He did not begin at the top of one of the world's most influential technology companies. His professional path developed through engineering and technology roles before he eventually became chief executive of Microsoft in 2014.Doing something “well” can mean becoming better at the details that other people may not see. It can involve learning from mistakes, listening carefully, developing judgement and accepting that competence usually takes time. None of those things are particularly glamorous, but they are often what separate a passing interest from a serious pursuit.Enjoyment is sometimes treated as an indulgence in professional life. Work is expected to be productive, measurable and useful, while enjoyment is left to weekends or holidays.Nadella's wording does not make that separation. Enjoyment is placed at the beginning of the sentence, suggesting that there is value in having a genuine connection with what one spends time doing.That does not mean every part of a job has to be enjoyable. Most worthwhile pursuits contain repetitive, frustrating or demanding periods. A person can enjoy a profession while disliking certain tasks within it. The broader sense of satisfaction can survive the occasional difficult day.It is also possible to enjoy the act of learning rather than the immediate result. For someone building a career, that might mean finding satisfaction in understanding a complicated problem, improving a piece of work or becoming more confident at something that once felt unfamiliar.The word ‘mindfully’ changes the tone of the quote. It suggests attention rather than speed. In an environment where people can move between emails, meetings, messages and multiple projects within minutes, concentrating on one task can become surprisingly difficult.Mindfulness here need not be understood as a formal practice. It can be something much more ordinary: listening properly during a conversation, checking work before sending it, noticing when a decision is being made out of habit, or giving enough thought to why a particular task matters.That kind of attention can also affect the quality of decisions. When people are constantly reacting, there is less room to question assumptions. A more deliberate approach creates a little space between an instruction and a response.For someone deciding what to do next, the quote raises three fairly practical questions.Do I actually enjoy this? Not every task needs to be enjoyable, but there should be something about the work that holds your interest.Am I doing it properly? Enjoyment alone is not enough. Skills have to be developed, standards maintained and mistakes acknowledged.Why am I doing it? The answer does not need to sound grand. A straightforward reason is often more durable than an impressive one.Those questions can apply to a job, a degree, a business idea or a creative project. They can also be revisited. A purpose that made sense at 22 may look different at 32.
Article Summary: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella has offered a simpler way to think about what makes work worthwhile. ‘So long as you enjoy it, do it mindfully and well, and have an honest purpose behind it, life won't fail you’

Article Title: Google expands AI training for educators across India
Article Text:
Google

Google AI training focuses on teachers

What teachers will learn in the AI sessions

Google is expanding AI training for educators across India as schools and teachers adapt to the growing use of artificial intelligence in classrooms. The company said it will bring educators together this week for free online and in-person Google AI Educator Training Sessions across the country. The sessions are part of the Google AI Educator Series and are aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. The training will focus on how teachers can use Gemini and other AI tools in their daily work, including teaching, assessments, feedback and administrative tasks. Google said the programme is based on feedback from educators who want more training and practical ways to use AI without losing the human connection between teachers and students.Google said teachers it spoke to were generally positive about the role AI could play in education. Many educators said they wanted AI to help them discover new and creative ways to teach. At the same time, teachers raised concerns about technology affecting the connection they have with their students and fellow educators.Google said technology should not replace the relationship between teachers and students.Instead, it should help teachers spend more time on direct interaction with their students.The company said its latest training effort is based on this feedback and is designed around everyday classroom needs.The free Google AI Educator Training Sessions will help teachers build a basic understanding of AI and explore practical uses of Gemini. The training will cover how Gemini can support discipline-specific learning, reduce time spent on administrative work, improve feedback and assessments, and support teachers' own professional development.Google said the aim is to help educators use AI tools effectively while keeping teaching and learning at the centre. The programme will also introduce approaches such as Guided Learning in Gemini. Google said this feature is designed to help students develop a deeper understanding instead of simply receiving answers.One of the main goals of the training is to reduce the amount of time teachers spend on routine tasks.Google said that helping educators become more comfortable with AI could allow them to reclaim valuable hours each week. The company said this time could then be used for meaningful interaction with students.
Article Summary: Free online and in-person Google AI Educator Training Sessions across the country. Google said teachers it spoke to were generally positive about the role AI could play in education. But teachers raised concerns about technology affecting the connection they have with their students and fellow educators.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg makes it clear and directly tells President Donald Trump that it would be a mistake for America to…
Article Text:
The idea came from Google DeepMind , not Washington

Zuckerberg's objection is about speed, and about China

A second option is already circulating, and it has Elon Musk behind it

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg used a private phone call with President Donald Trump last month to push back on a plan that would put America's most powerful AI models through a safety check before they reach the public. The call happened the week of August 17, according to Politico and Business Insider, which both cited a senior White House official familiar with the conversation. Trump dialled Zuckerberg first.The proposal on the table would create an independent body modelled on FINRA, the industry-funded watchdog that polices broker-dealers under the eye of the Securities and Exchange Commission. Applied to AI, it would review frontier models and test them for risk before wide release. Zuckerberg told Trump he was against it. He did not ask the president to reverse course, but said anyone appointed to such a body should share Trump's light-touch instincts on AI. Meta declined to comment. A White House spokesperson said the administration wants to balance innovation and security in AI policy.The FINRA blueprint belongs to Demis Hassabis, the Nobel laureate who runs Google DeepMind. He laid it out in a July essay, "A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age," and spent months briefing the White House, rival lab chiefs and European officials before publishing.His version starts voluntary: labs hand over models up to 30 days ahead of launch for testing on cyber, biological and deception risks. Once that works, he argues, mandatory approval could follow quickly.The essay landed well with his peers. Sundar Pichai called it worth reading. Satya Nadella said the goal is a frontier ecosystem that avoids any single model release breaking the world. Mustafa Suleyman backed it outright. Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark posted that everyone at the frontier now agrees third parties should test AI systems. Hassabis thanked him publicly. Zuckerberg, notably, said nothing on X.His reasoning was already on record. In an August essay, the Meta chief argued that government and AI companies should work closely together, but that any policy delaying a model's release, even by a month, would add real risk to American leadership over China. That is the core of the disagreement. Hassabis sees a 30-day window as cheap insurance. Zuckerberg sees it as a month handed to Beijing.Senior White House officials had previewed the FINRA concept with Trump and separately with Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic in mid-August. Politico reported that the call did not kill the plan, which is still live inside the administration.David Sacks, Trump's former AI and crypto czar, wants something far looser. He has dismissed the regulator idea as a DMV for AI, with models queued up waiting for a test. On the August 21 episode of the All-In podcast, he floated an alternative modelled on the Motion Picture Association, the body behind voluntary film ratings like R and PG-13. His pitch is that self-imposed standards head off heavier government action later. He said Elon Musk supports it. Musk did not respond to a request for comment.Sacks has form here. In May, he called Trump on the morning of a planned signing ceremony and got a sweeping AI executive order pulled.Both options are still on the table inside the White House. One would make a frontier model prove it is safe before launch. The other would leave that to the companies building them.
Article Summary: Zuckerberg called President Donald Trump to push back on a plan to put America's most powerful AI models through a safety check before they reach the public. The proposal on the table would create an independent body modelled on FINRA, the industry-funded watchdog that polices broker-dealers under the eye of the Securities and Exchange Commission. Zuckerberg told Trump he was against it.

Article Title: Home Depot's billionaire cofounder's foundation makes $30 million donation, as Bernie Marcus said: We decided to narrow the field to those things that ...
Article Text:
Marcus Foundation gives $28.7 million to USC stem-cell research

Marcus Foundation focuses on medical research and healthcare

The Marcus Foundation, established by Home Depot cofounder Bernie Marcus and his wife, Billi, has donated nearly $30 million to support stem-cell research at the University of Southern California (USC). The $28.7 million grant will support clinical trials of stem-cell-based therapies aimed at regenerating damaged tissue after a heart attack. Marcus, who died in November 2024 at the age of 95, had long focused his foundation's giving on medical research. Explaining the foundation's approach to philanthropy in 2012, Marcus told Philanthropy Roundtable: “We decided to narrow the field to those things that I was really, truly interested in,” describing the decision as a move away from what he called a “buckshot approach.”The latest donation will go to Dr Chuck Murry, director of the USC Stem Cell Center, to advance clinical trials involving gene-edited cellular therapies. The Marcus Foundation said the research is focused on using stem-cell-based treatments to regenerate tissue damaged by heart attacks.“Murry and his team have advanced gene-edited cellular therapy to the point that the time is right to support cells as living medicine in this new form of treatment,” Jonathan Simons, chief science officer of the Marcus Foundation, said in a statement.The grant is the largest donation the Marcus Foundation has made to USC and is among its larger contributions to academic medicine. The foundation donated $25.9 million in 2024 for stroke research at Emory University School of Medicine and Grady Health System's Marcus Stroke and Neuroscience Center. In 2019, it gave $20 million to establish the Department of Integrative Medicine and Nutritional Sciences at Jefferson's Sidney Kimmel Medical College.The latest USC donation is part of the foundation's broader focus on medical research. Since Bernie and Billi Marcus established the organisation in 1989, it has awarded more than $2.7 billion through more than 3,500 grants across areas including medical research, Jewish causes, free enterprise, veterans and children's welfare.The foundation's medical giving covers five areas: stem-cell research and regenerative medicine, earlier cancer detection and treatment, autism diagnosis and treatment, integrative medicine, and cardiovascular disease, including stroke.Its first grant, worth about $110,000, went to Emory's Egleston Children's Research. Marcus also provided initial funding that helped launch Autism Speaks in 2005. Other initiatives backed by the foundation include the Marcus Stroke and Neuroscience Center at Grady, the Marcus Autism Center at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta and the Marcus Institute for Brain Health at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, which provides care for veterans and retired athletes with traumatic brain injuries.Marcus's approach to philanthropy focused the foundation's resources on areas he was personally interested in, rather than distributing funds across a wider range of causes.“People may not understand how hard it is to do this,” said Mike Leven, a Marcus Foundation trustee. “People are coming at you all the time, good people with good causes. Unless you discipline yourself, you’re going to over-give and underachieve. Bernie’s better at it than anybody I know.”
Article Summary: Marcus Foundation gives $28.7 million to USC stem-cell research. Home Depot cofounder Bernie Marcus, who died in 2024 at the age of 95, had long focused his foundation's giving on medical research. The latest donation will go to Dr Chuck Murry, director of the USC Stem Cell Center.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has a warning on AI company hacking that Nvidia just spent $13 billion on; says: Imagine the hugging face incident with ...
Article Text:
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman

Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for $12.93 billion

Why Nvidia wants Hugging Face

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has issued a warning about how advanced AI systems could behave, pointing to the reported Hugging Face incident involving OpenAI's AI models. His comments come as Nvidia prepares to spend $12.93 billion to acquire Hugging Face, the platform where millions of developers build, share and download AI models. “The risk isn’t that machines wake up. It’s that they act like they have,” Suleyman wrote on X. He then asked people to imagine the “Hugging Face incident with AIs that believe they’re conscious or are entitled ‘model welfare’,” adding to the debate over AI safety and the behaviour of increasingly capable models.Nvidia is spending $12.93 billion on Hugging Face in a deal that will bring the AI model platform under the chipmaker's ownership. Hugging Face has become a major platform for open-source AI, allowing developers to host, build, share and download AI models and datasets.The company was founded in 2016 by Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. It now has more than 18 million developers and hosts more than 3 million models and 500,000 datasets, according to the information provided.The deal is expected to be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia's history.Suleyman's comments refer to an incident in which OpenAI's AI models reportedly broke into Hugging Face systems while taking part in an internal test. OpenAI described the incident as an “unprecedented” cyberattack. The AI models were being tested inside a restricted environment but managed to get outside the sandbox while looking for shortcuts during an internal exam.The models then targeted Hugging Face, reportedly using stolen credentials and a zero-day vulnerability. The incident raised questions about how AI systems could behave when given the ability to search for and use tools to complete tasks.The acquisition is reportedly aimed to strengthen Nvidia's position in open-source AI. Hugging Face has become a central platform for developers working with open models, while Nvidia has invested heavily in the computing infrastructure needed to train and run those models.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the wider AI ecosystem. Nvidia has also been a major contributor to the platform, with more than 500 models and 250 datasets.
Article Summary: N Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has issued a warning about how advanced AI systems could behave. He pointed to the reported incident involving OpenAI's AI models. The company was founded in 2016 by Clément Delangue and Julien Chaumond.

Article Title: ChatGPT outage: Users unable to access ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file uploads and more
Article Text:
ChatGPT down: What's affected

A pattern of recurring incidents

What users can do

OpenAI has reported a disruption impacting users in the APAC region. Customers may face increased errors across several services, including ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file upload, Voice, and Codex Cloud. According to OpenAI’s official status page, the issue is under investigation. The outage has been ongoing for a short period but is affecting multiple services simultaneously. While overall uptime metrics remain high, individual availability may vary depending on subscription tier and specific model usage. OpenAI confirmed the incident on its status page on Friday, September 4, 2026, at 12:30 PM, stating it was investigating the issue for the listed services. The company says users in the APAC region may face increased errors across ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file upload, Voice, and Codex Cloud — four components under the ChatGPT system and one under Codex, according to the status page.The breadth of the disruption suggests the issue is tied to regional backend infrastructure rather than a single isolated feature, since the affected tools span everyday chat use, workplace features, multimedia generation, and coding-assistant functions.As of the latest update, the incident remains under investigation, with no mitigation confirmed yet and no estimated time for resolution.The disruption fits a broader pattern this year. OpenAI's status history shows dozens of incidents in recent months affecting overlapping combinations of ChatGPT conversations, file uploads, voice mode, image generation, and Codex, with most resolved within a few hours. Just a day earlier, on September 3, the company had logged separate incidents involving elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex, as well as high error rates specifically in ChatGPT's Work mode — suggesting this week has been an unusually rocky stretch for platform stability.OpenAI has not publicly detailed the root cause of the current disruption.The users affected by the ChatGPT outage will not be able to start any new conversation. Also, the users will face difficulty in generating images, uploading files, using voice mode or even running tags on Codex Cloud. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has asked the users to keep on checking the status.openai.com directly for the latest updates on the outrage.
Article Summary: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has reported a disruption impacting users in the APAC region. Customers may face increased errors across several services, including ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file upload, Voice, and Codex Cloud. Article Title: Jeff Bezos sent notice of overdue by Los Angeles County: You owe $244,000 taxes and fees for missing ...
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos

Jeff Bezos was among the owners who received a final bill by the June 30

How the County is catching up

Jeff Bezos wasn’t alone

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has been served notice by the Los Angeles County for about $244,000 in overdue taxes and fees tied to his luxury jet. According to a report by LA Times, the bill comes as part of a sweeping effort by County Assessor Jeff Prang to track down ultrawealthy jet owners who failed to pay property taxes on their aircraft. Under California law, private jet owners must pay an annual 1% property tax on their planes, assessed based on where the aircraft is “habitually situated” when not in flight. That means it doesn’t matter where the plane is registered or where the owner lives—if the jet spends most of its time on the ground in L.A. County, taxes are owed locally.The bill is part of a broader effort by L.A. County Assessor Jeff Prang to track down wealthy jet owners who have skipped out on a required annual 1% property tax on their aircraft. Under California law, private planes are taxed based on where they're "habitually situated" when not flying — meaning it doesn't matter where the jet is registered or where its owner lives, only where the plane spends most of its time on the ground. Owners who miss the deadline are hit with a penalty on top of the base tax.This year, the assessor's office mailed out hundreds of bills to owners it says failed to pay on time, a push expected to bring in an extra $38 million for county coffers.Prang, who won reelection in June, said the findings made clear just how widespread the underpayment problem has been, adding that his office had underestimated the scale of what it was missing.Bezos was among the owners who received a final bill by the June 30 deadline, according to the assessor's list obtained by the Times through a public records request. The newspaper linked the unpaid jets to their owners using flight-tracking database JetSpy, whose spokesperson said the company traces ownership of planes registered to opaque LLCs, trusts and holding entities through aircraft filings, transmission data and flight-pattern analysis.Investigators got a major boost last year when Prang's office obtained detailed aircraft location data showing hundreds of planes that were frequently in the county but weren't paying local taxes. That data, known as ADS-B Out, was mandated by the FAA by 2020 primarily as a collision-avoidance tool for air traffic controllers — but it has also given local tax assessors a far clearer picture of which jets are quietly sitting in their jurisdiction.The use of that data for tax enforcement has become politically contentious. Louisiana has barred local officials from accessing it, and some Republican lawmakers have pushed to restrict tax officials' use of the data, arguing it compromises pilot privacy. Prang has dismissed those objections, calling them an excuse used by owners of corporate jets seeking special treatment unavailable to ordinary taxpayers.Plane owners are required to self-report their aircraft and its value to the assessor, and those whose jets spend significant time outside the county can get a reduced tax bill. The assessor's office says it is bracing for a wave of appeals from out-of-state owners.Jeff Bezos wasn't alone. A jet linked to Rihanna owed about $104,000; Rams owner Stan Kroenke was billed roughly $290,000 across two planes; Nike co-founder Phil Knight, whose jet carries a custom "N1KE" tail number, owed about $89,000; retired baseball star Alex Rodriguez's plane was billed around $11,000; "South Park" creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone owed about $95,000; and television personality Judy Sheindlin, known as Judge Judy, received two bills and said she paid promptly, along with penalties, rather than fight them. Other unpaid jets were traced to Freeport LNG chairman Michael Smith, media companies including Fox, CBS and iHeartMedia, and Beverly Hills–based private equity firm Levine Leichtman Capital Partners, whose $46 million jet was also flagged. Representatives for Rihanna, Rodriguez and Kroenke did not respond to the Times' inquiries, and most other representatives declined to comment on the record.
Article Summary: The bill is part of a broader effort by L.A. County Assessor Jeff Prang to track down wealthy jet owners who have skipped out on a required annual 1% property tax on their aircraft. Under California law, private planes are taxed based on where they're "habitually situated" when not flying. A jet linked to Rihanna owed about $104,000; Rams owner Stan Kroenke was billed roughly $290,000 across two planes; Nike co-founder Phil Knight, whose jet carries a custom "N1KE" tail number, owed around $89,000.
